Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a continuous lucent line outlining the aortic knuckle and mediastinal structures, which is the hallmark radiographic sign of pneumomediastinum. In the context of a cavitating lesion (such as invasive aspergillosis), this finding indicates that the cavity has eroded into the mediastinum rather than the pericardial sac (which would present as pneumopericardium).
